preamble: Palatalization of the alveolar stop [t] to the palatal stop [c]. In Czech and Slovak, Proto-Slavic *t became palatal ť [c] before front vowels (*i, *ě, and in Slovak also *e), so that Czech tichý is [ˈcɪxiː] and Slovak deti is [ˈɟeci]; the orthography still writes ⟨ti, tě⟩ for [ci, cɛ]. In Hungarian, a word-final /t/ assimilates to a following palatal stop /c/ across a morpheme or word boundary, as in hat tyúk [hɒc‿cuːk] 'six hens'.

examples.note: Inherited *t before *i became palatal ť, written ⟨t⟩ before ⟨i⟩.
Before *ě the same palatal ť arose; Old Czech is reconstructed as /ˈci̯ɛɫo/.
Final *ti became [ci]; the initial *d shows the parallel change to [ɟ].
Both the medial and the final *t became palatal before *i.
Partial palatal assimilation of /t/ before the palatal stop /c/; optional in careful speech.
